sections.overview: Limnognathia maerski is a microscopic freshwater animal and one of only two described species in the phylum Micrognathozoa; the other is L. desmeti.
sections.identification: Adults are about 0.1–0.15 millimetres long and have a body divided into head, accordion-like thorax and abdomen. Its remarkably complex mouthparts include many tiny hardened jaw elements.
sections.habitat: It was first found among submerged moss at a cold spring on Disko Island, Greenland; later records include cold freshwater habitats in the Pyrenees.
sections.diet: It feeds on decomposing plant material and bacterial films, which are grasped and processed by different parts of its complex jaw apparatus.
sections.behavior: Cilia let it glide over surfaces and swim briefly through the water; a ventral adhesive pad helps it attach to the substrate.
sections.reproduction: Only females have been found, so parthenogenesis is presumed; the reproductive cycle is not fully understood.
sections.ecology: In a 2025 study, the Greenland and Pyrenean populations remained within L. maerski, while the genetically distinct Crozet population was described as L. desmeti; no visible morphological difference separated them.
sections.conservation: Its microscopic size and scattered records make its distribution difficult to assess; the sources reviewed do not establish a global conservation status or population trend.
